Subject: VectorFlux - GPU allocation assertion & ops checklist

Team —

VectorFlux is into final legal review and wants a firm sense of what we can provision if they commit (probable close in late Nov). They asked for a 'confirmed allocation' that ties to a 12-month Dedicated commitment. I want to propose a provisional allocation so Sales can include it in the MSA appendix. Please do a quick signals check on the fleet and confirm whether we can assert the following:

- Requested capacity: 48 x A100-equivalent concurrent slots (max seq 2k) for initial ramp; additionally reserve 8 x 4-bit quant nodes for burst inference.
- Expected start: onboarding window week of 2026-11-15
- Duration: 12 months rolling start from onboarding

Action items:
- Karthik: run an availability snapshot across us-west-2 and us-east-1, call out any maintenance windows or fleet refreshes that would block an assertion. Recommend a conservative allocation to include for the MSA.
- Marissa: confirm whether thermal/psu constraints in our us-west pools change per-slot capacity for 2k seq. If we can't do full A100-equivalent density, propose the quantized fallback and estimated perf delta.

I've attached the deal brief from Sales and a rough placeholder capacity matrix (capacity_matrix_q4_v2.xlsx). Need responses by EOD Tuesday so I can draft the appendix.

Thanks —
Diego

Diego —

Quick snapshot after checking current reservations, maintenance calendar, and planned model-onboarding jobs:

Summary (conservative):
- Us-west-2 dedicated pools: nominal capacity for 40 A100-eq concurrent slots available starting 2026-11-10; however a planned node firmware rollout 2026-11-12—11/13 could reduce effective throughput by ~8 slots for two days. Recommend we don't promise those two days in the appendix.
- Us-east-1: spare capacity for ~16 A100-eq slots but requires a cross-region routing policy (adds ~12–28 ms p50 depending on instance).
- Quantized 4-bit nodes: we can provision 8 low-precision nodes in us-west-2 immediately; throughput looks good for their burst profile.

Recommendation:
- Assert a conservative committed allocation of 40 A100-eq slots in us-west-2 (primary) + 8 quant nodes as burst pool. Call out: firmware rollout on 11/12–11/13 as an exception in appendix.
- Add a fallback policy: if us-west-2 capacity dips, route non-latency-critical traffic to us-east-1 with a defined latency SLO bump.

I've uploaded an annotated capacity matrix to the Drive link. If Sales wants to request a hard hold (meaning we earmark nodes and block other commitments) we need exec approval because that reduces our flexibility; it would also carry a 6–8% surcharge for reservation insurance.

-Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-20 08:45 PDT
Subject: Re: VectorFlux - GPU allocation assertion & ops checklist

Diego / Karthik —

A couple of operational notes to fold into the appendix:

- Thermal & rack density: the specific us-west-2 racks we usually pull from are at 86–90% thermal headroom when running sustained 2k-sequence loads. That means unless we split the workload across additional racks (which requires cross-pod network setup), we will see CPU-side contention for IO (not GPU). Operationally this increases the risk of tail latency spikes during their heaviest batch windows.
- Workaround: for sustained loads we should recommend either (a) burst to quant nodes for non-critical requests or (b) a split-traffic ingest that buffers larger requests and serves smaller ones on hot-path A100-eq. Option (a) is simpler and can be included in the MSA.
- Onboarding runway: our standard Dedicated onboarding (networking, KMS, audit logs) is 12–18 business days once we have a signed PO + security questionnaire completed. If they need faster, we can do a compressed plan (10 business days) but will require a dedicated success engineer and an onboarding fee.

If Sales wants the hard hold, we need to confirm surcharge, and Ops needs a two-week visibility window to shift capacity. My preference: assert 40 slots + 8 quant burst, and include the compressed-onboarding option as a priced line item.

—Marissa
Principal Cloud Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops_runbook_excerpt.txt (3 KB)]

Elena —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Per our discussion I wanted to put the proposed next steps in writing so legal can align the appendix language with operational reality. We are prepared to provisionally assert the following, subject to a signed PO and standard security clearance:

Provisional allocation (non-exclusive assertion for inclusion in MSA appendix):
- 40 A100-equivalent concurrent slots in us-west-2 (primary)
- 8 x 4-bit quant nodes reserved for burst inference
- Planned start: onboarding window week of 2026-11-15
- Duration: 12 months rolling from go-live

Key exceptions & notes:
- Maintenance window: firmware rollout on 2026-11-12–11/13 may impact capacity. We will exclude those dates from any guaranteed availability period in the appendix.
- Onboarding: standard 12–18 business days; compressed path (10 business days) available for an onboarding fee.
- Reservation surcharge: hard hold (true capacity earmark) carries a reservation insurance surcharge (approx. 6–8%).

Next steps:
1) If this aligns with your expectations, can you share a non-binding PO by EOD 2026-10-25? We will then open a provisional allocation request and schedule onboarding kickoff.
2) Complete the security questionnaire (I attached the worksheet).
3) Sign the mutual action plan (link below) so Legal/Finance can run the MSA appendix through the cadence.

Draft MAP & PO template attached. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/MutualAction/VF-2026-1472

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the exceptions.

Best —
Diego Fernandez
